messages:
Maria G: quick question — thinking about 'priority plugging' to use short unused slack capacity windows by routing low-risk probation tenants into a bounded plug during bursts. Sketch below.

Jordan: curious. what's the plug boundary? how do we avoid creating new attack vector where clients send small cheap calls to game priority?

Maria G: idea: probabilistic admission with a per-tenant plug budget that decays; plug window caps per-minute; score based on recent abuse signals. plug only when global utilization > 80% and high-priority backlog > X.

Sam K: I like decaying budget. We need deterministic fallback for model-critical paths. Also telemetry: per-tenant plug_accept_rate, avg_latency_delta when plugged.

Leo: operational concern: added jitter from toggling plug on/off may mess with tail latency SLO. Can we smooth transitions with a 10s ramp? or maintain KV cache affinity during plug periods?

Maria G: ramping sounds right. ramp_seconds = 10 default. KV affinity: keep same routing so cache cold starts are minimized.

Jordan: abuse side — we must ensure plug admission is priced/penalized. Maybe increment an abuse_score on every plugged acceptance and apply stronger throttles if score rises.

Sam K: proposal: update our admission proto with fields: plug_window_ms, plug_budget, plug_decay_half_life. Also expose feature flag per-namespace and a dry-run metric.

Maria G: pseudocode:
```
if global_util > 0.8 and tenant.plug_budget > 0:
  admit = random() < tenant.plug_budget / max_budget
  if admit: tenant.plug_budget -= 1
```

Leo: sounds fine. also add a hard cap: no tenant can consume > 5% of plug capacity per minute.

Jordan: action items: (1) write RFC sketch with telemetry table; (2) run sim against synthetic abuse patterns; (3) small lab rollout with feature flag and dry-run telemetry.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: rfc/drafts/priority-plugging at 09:00 PT tomorrow (reminder set)

Maria G: thanks — I'll draft and ping for an async review. :thumbsup:
